item.title: What Happens When the Ski Slopes Become Your Front Door?
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
In Oberlech, a car-free village high in Austria’s Arlberg, winter begins where the road ends. Once snow arrives, the village is accessible only by cable car, placing Burg Hotel Lech at 1,650 meters in the heart of one of the Alps’ most celebrated ski regions. Surrounded by 300 kilometers of interconnected slopes, the hotel offers true ski-in, ski-out access, allowing guests to move from their room to the mountain without the logistics that can turn a ski vacation into a production.

The experience continues well after the lifts close. At Burg Eisbar No. 1, a slope-side ice bar with a heated terrace, retractable roof and live music, après-ski can stretch into the evening. For a more traditional Alpine atmosphere, Burg Schenke serves fondue in a rustic tavern setting, while the adults-only Burg Oasis offers a quieter retreat with a stone pine sauna, snow cabin and fireplace whirlpool. Together, the spaces give a stay at Burg Hotel Lech several distinct ways to experience winter, from first tracks on the mountain to a slower evening indoors.

The Curated Take: The appeal of Burg Hotel Lech is the way its setting shapes the entire stay. The car-free village and ski-in, ski-out access eliminate much of the friction associated with a mountain getaway, while the hotel’s après-ski, dining and wellness spaces create reasons to linger once skiing is over. It is a distinctly Alpine version of luxury where convenience comes from being completely immersed in the landscape.

item.title: Could Thailand Be the Winter Reset You Didn’t Know You Needed?
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
When winter starts to feel less like a season and more like something to escape, Hua Hin, Thailand offers a warmer alternative. About three hours from Bangkok, the unhurried coastal destination is home to Chiva-Som Hua Hin, a pioneering wellness resort that has spent more than 30 years developing a highly personalized approach to wellbeing. With warm temperatures, clear skies and low humidity during the winter months, Hua Hin provides a natural setting for travelers looking to step away from colder weather and reset.

Set across seven acres of tropical gardens, Chiva-Som combines wellness programs and treatments with fresh, organic cuisine and daily movement classes. Each stay begins with a consultation with a Health and Wellness Advisor, allowing guests to shape their experience around individual wellness goals rather than following a one-size-fits-all program. The resort also maintains phone-free public spaces, creating an environment designed to encourage guests to disconnect from the pace and distractions of everyday life. The result is a tropical retreat where the setting, expert guidance and daily rhythm all contribute to a more intentional wellness escape.

The Curated Take: The appeal here is less about escaping winter for a few days and more about changing the rhythm of a trip altogether. Chiva-Som’s combination of personalized guidance, tropical surroundings and intentional disconnection reflects the growing appeal of wellness travel that feels immersive rather than simply adding a spa treatment to a conventional vacation. For luxury travelers seeking restoration as much as recreation, the ability to build a stay around individual goals makes the experience particularly relevant.

item.title: What If Your Winter Escape Took You to the Galápagos?
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
When winter arrives, the Galápagos Islands offer a very different kind of escape: sun-warmed volcanic landscapes, pristine beaches and wildlife encounters in one of the world’s most distinctive ecosystems. This year, Ecuadorian expedition company Quasar Expeditions marks 40 years of exploring the archipelago, with small-scale cruises aboard the newly renovated Quasar Evolution, accommodating 32 guests, and Quasar Grace, with space for just 16. Eight- and 15-day itineraries combine the comforts of a yacht with the opportunity to venture well beyond the most accessible corners of the islands.

Days unfold through hiking, snorkeling, kayaking and paddleboarding, with encounters that can include sea lions, whale sharks, sea turtles, flamingos, Darwin’s finches and blue-footed boobies. The smaller vessels allow Quasar to reach remote sites, outer islands and secluded coves that are less accessible to larger ships, while expert-led excursions place the emphasis on understanding the endemic species and unusual landscapes that make the Galápagos such an important destination for naturalists and curious travelers alike.

The Curated Take: The Galápagos has always been about the encounter, but the scale of the vessel changes the character of the journey. With only 16 or 32 guests aboard, the experience has the intimacy of a private expedition while retaining access to expert interpretation and carefully planned excursions. For luxury travelers seeking warmth during the winter months, the appeal is not simply escaping the cold, but trading it for a destination where nearly every day offers a deeper look at a living ecosystem that cannot be replicated elsewhere.

item.title: What Does Christmas Look Like on a Private Island in the Maldives?
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
At Baros Maldives in the North Malé Atoll, the festive season trades snow-covered streets for palms, turquoise water and celebrations designed around the island itself. Rather than treating Christmas and New Year’s as a single gala event, the resort builds a season of shared experiences, beginning with a cocktail reception at The Lighthouse and continuing with a Christmas Eve Gala Dinner at Lime. As the year draws to a close, another cocktail reception leads into the New Year’s Eve Gala Dinner and countdown.

The celebrations extend beyond the formal occasions. An Island Christmas Market brings a festive touch to the tropical setting, while hands-on experiences give guests opportunities to interact with one another in a more relaxed atmosphere. A Christmas cookie workshop, cooking class focused on Maldivian seafood and cocktail-making sessions add local flavor and participation to the holiday calendar, creating experiences that are as much about gathering as they are about dining and entertainment.

The Curated Take: A holiday escape to the Maldives can easily become an exercise in seclusion, which makes Baros’ approach particularly interesting. The resort is using the festive season to create moments of connection without turning the island into a conventional holiday resort. The combination of intimate celebrations, hands-on experiences and Maldivian culinary influences offers luxury travelers a way to mark the holidays somewhere dramatically different while still preserving the sense of escape that makes the Maldives so compelling.

item.title: Rockpool Bar & Grill Perth Set for a $3 Million Transformation
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
One of Perth’s established dining institutions is getting a substantial refresh. Rockpool Bar & Grill at Crown Perth will temporarily close October 4 before reopening October 28 following a $3 million transformation. The fifteen-year-old restaurant will receive a redesigned bar as well as upgrades to its dining room and private spaces, while retaining the wood-fired grill, open kitchen and produce-driven menu that have defined the restaurant since its opening.

The renovation signals a new chapter for one of the city’s best-known premium dining venues without abandoning the elements that established its identity. For visitors staying at Crown Perth or exploring the city’s high-end restaurant scene, the refreshed restaurant will offer a familiar name in a newly designed setting.

The Curated Take:
Restaurant renovations can sometimes mean a complete reinvention, but Rockpool’s approach is more about refinement. Keeping the open kitchen, wood-fired grill and Australian produce at the center while reworking the spaces suggests a refresh designed to bring the restaurant into its next era without erasing what made it recognizable.

item.title: What If You Could Experience Venice Carnival From the Inside?
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Venice Carnival takes on a more intimate character at Violino d’Oro, where guests can experience one of Italy’s most celebrated traditions through local craftsmanship, private access and insider connections. Located in the heart of Venice, the hotel is offering a Carnival experience from January 30 through February 9 that begins with a visit to a Venetian atelier and a meeting with local designer Antonia Sautter. Guests can learn about the artistry behind the costumes before selecting a customized, made-to-measure Carnival dress, with Violino d’Oro arranging the fittings, water taxi transfers and access to one of Venice’s prestigious themed Carnival balls.

The experience continues beyond the costume with private entry to Palazzo Ducale and the prisons associated with Casanova’s famous escape, tea at the historic Caffè Florian, and a masked photoshoot through Venice’s canals aboard a gondola. Guests can also take part in a cocktail class at Il Piccolo Bar, creating an itinerary that connects the spectacle of Carnival with the craftsmanship, history and traditions of Venice itself. Rather than simply attending Carnival, the experience offers travelers the opportunity to encounter the festival through the people and places that give it its distinctive character.

The Curated Take: What makes this experience compelling is the access behind the spectacle. Carnival is one of Venice’s most recognizable traditions, but Violino d’Oro builds an itinerary around the creative process and local relationships that exist beneath the masks and costumes. Meeting a Venetian designer, commissioning a personalized look and gaining access to historic and cultural sites creates a more layered way to experience Venice during Carnival, particularly for luxury travelers who value craftsmanship, storytelling and connections with the destination.

item.title: What Happens When an Alpine Ski Resort Becomes a Winter Wellness Retreat?
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Winter at Forsthofgut Nature Hotel in Leogang, Austria, extends well beyond the ski slopes. Set in the Austrian Alps with ski-in/ski-out access to the Saalbach Hinterglemm Leogang Fieberbrunn ski area, the luxury nature hotel puts guests within reach of approximately 168 miles of slopes while also offering snowshoeing, tobogganing and a new ice rink debuting this winter. The experience shifts indoors after a day in the snow, where the expansive 61,000-square-foot waldSPA features panoramic saunas, indoor and outdoor pools and an onsen-style pool overlooking the surrounding landscape.

Wellness is equally central to the resort’s winter offering. At waldSPA Health, guests can explore treatments and experiences including cryotherapy and altitude training, while the Mountain Loft Suites provide a more secluded retreat with private terraces, saunas and hot tubs overlooking the snow-covered Leoganger Steinberge. The result is an Alpine escape that pairs the active pleasures of winter in Leogang, Austria, with the increasingly sought-after luxury of having somewhere restorative to retreat when the day outside is done.

The Curated Take: Forsthofgut is interesting because it treats winter as more than a season for skiing. The combination of access to a major Alpine ski area, an unusually expansive spa, specialized wellness experiences and private suites with their own saunas and hot tubs gives travelers multiple ways to experience the mountains. For luxury travelers who want the drama of the Austrian Alps without spending every hour on the slopes, that balance of adventure, nature and restoration is part of the appeal.

item.title: What If You Could Have a Swiss Mountain All to Yourself?
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
High above Lake St. Moritz in St. Moritz, Switzerland, the five-star, all-suite Carlton Hotel St. Moritz offers a winter escape built around both the glamour and the quieter pleasures of the Engadine. Guests can explore the snowy landscape by horse-drawn carriage, husky sled, ice skate across the frozen lake or venture out with the hotel’s Outdoor Butler, who can arrange everything from a personalized ski tour to a snow trek through the surrounding mountains. The resort’s setting also puts travelers within easy reach of the designer boutiques and polished atmosphere of St. Moritz, one of Switzerland’s most renowned winter destinations.

For an experience that takes exclusivity a step further, the hotel’s Rent a Mountain experience gives guests private access to an illuminated ski slope and gondola for an evening on the mountain without the usual crowds. Back at the hotel, the experience can continue with a private Fondue Gondola or time spent unwinding at the Bel Etage. It is a distinctly St. Moritz approach to winter travel: alpine adventure, après-ski indulgence and the kind of privacy that turns a snowy escape into something truly memorable.

The Curated Take: The appeal of Carlton Hotel St. Moritz is not simply its access to winter sports, but the range of ways it allows travelers to experience the Swiss Alps on their own terms. The combination of a personal Outdoor Butler, private mountain access and refined après-ski experiences creates a version of St. Moritz that feels less like checking off a list of winter activities and more like having the landscape arranged around you. For luxury travelers seeking both iconic Alpine scenery and meaningful exclusivity, that distinction is significant.

item.title: Perth Welcomes a New British Pub With The Queen’s Arms
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
A traditional British pub is returning to Perth’s CBD with the opening of The Queen’s Arms in a heritage-listed, three-level building on Queen Street. The 500-capacity venue features two bars with more than 30 taps, multiple dining areas, an elevated beer garden and rooftop terrace, with a menu centered on British pub classics alongside Australian favorites. The opening marks the return of a traditional British pub to the heart of Perth after nearly a decade.

The project comes from hospitality group Nokturnl, whose portfolio includes venues at Yagan Square, and gives the city’s evolving dining scene another large-scale social destination. Its combination of historic architecture, pub culture and multiple indoor and outdoor spaces is designed to make it as much a gathering place as a restaurant.

The Curated Take:
The Queen’s Arms is an interesting example of how a city can embrace a familiar cultural idea while giving it a distinctly local setting. The heritage building, Australian ingredients and Perth location keep the concept from feeling like a replica transported wholesale from Britain.
